main_body: A wide wooden unit seen straight on, made of three stacked horizontal planks or boxes with grey stone showing between them. The top and bottom ones are plain plank fronts, and the middle one is a framed box holding barrels and an orange item.
top_band: none. At x=15, row 0 is an outline (L=60), row 1 is a single slightly lighter row (L=98), and rows 2-3 (L=64) are the same family as the face. That is a 1px highlight, not a top surface.
evidence: Each of the three parts is a vertical face. In the top plank the only light row is a 1px highlight (row 1) over rows 2-3 of the same brown, closed by a dark row 4. The middle box has a thin 1-row light edge at row 7, then dark rows 8-10 and a mid-brown face (rows 12-15). It shows no horizontal surface seen from above, and the barrels and orange item are painted flat on the face rather than inset. The bottom plank has the same 1px highlight, then rows of similar tone. This matches the red 'front elevation: top 1' example in the guide, so the drawing fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The brown wood ramp has about 5 steps (dark outline, deep brown, mid, light, highlight), with grain dots and a speckled stone background. The measured facts support this: 18 colours per tile against 17 and 20 in the references, 0% flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted brown rather than near-black. It has fewer distinct colours overall (18 against 38-40), but it is a smaller piece, and per-tile richness matches the references. It would sit acceptably beside them.
